title: Tümed
capsule: The Tümed were a Mongol tribal polity centered in the Hohhot basin of Inner Mongolia, rising to prominence under Altan Khan (r. 1543–1582), who unified the southern Mongolian tribes and conducted regular raids deep into northern China, forcing the Ming dynasty to agree to border markets in 1571 — the first formal Sino-Mongolian trade treaty in over a century. Altan Khan also invited the Third Dalai Lama, Sonam Gyatso, to his court in 1578, conferring the title 'Dalai Lama' and cementing the Gelug-Mongol religious alliance that would define later Mongolian Buddhism. After Altan Khan's death the Tümed gradually fragmented; the Qing dynasty incorporated their territories as banners under the Eight Banners system by the late seventeenth century, with formal subjugation completed by 1699.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Tümed's core territory in the Hohhot basin is well documented by Chinese border records and Mongolian chronicles; the lateral steppe extent under Altan Khan's suzerainty is reconstructed from tribute and campaign records and is approximate.
